purpose: This medication is used to treat Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in adults and children aged 6 and older. It is also approved to treat moderate to severe binge eating disorder in adults. It helps improve focus, attention, and control impulsive behavior.
how_it_works: Lisdexamfetamine is a prodrug, which means your body converts it into an active form called dextroamphetamine after you swallow it. This active form increases the levels of certain natural chemicals in your brain, like dopamine and norepinephrine, which help with focus and self-control. Because your body has to convert it first, it works more gradually and steadily than some other stimulants.
common_side_effects: Decreased appetite and weight loss, trouble sleeping, dry mouth, headache, increased heart rate, stomach upset or nausea, feeling irritable or anxious, and dizziness. Many of these are more noticeable when you first start the medication.
warnings: This is a controlled substance with a potential for abuse and dependence, so never share it with others. It can raise your blood pressure and heart rate, so tell your doctor if you have heart problems. It may cause or worsen psychiatric symptoms like anxiety, hallucinations, or mood changes. Do not take it if you have taken an MAO inhibitor in the last 14 days, as this can cause a dangerous reaction. Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or have a history of substance abuse.
typical_dosing: For ADHD, adults and children typically start at 30 mg once every morning. The dose can be adjusted by your doctor up to a maximum of 70 mg per day. It is taken by mouth once a day in the morning — taking it later in the day can make it hard to sleep. You can swallow the capsule whole or open it and mix the powder into water, yogurt, or orange juice.
